name: Aromanian
variety: Aromanian as written in the orthography with ã, dz, lj, nj, sh, ts; a general description drawn from the dialect studies, without one standard variety
sources: Capidan, Theodor (1932). Aromânii: dialectul aromân. Studiu lingvistic. București: Academia Română.
Caragiu Marioțeanu, Matilda (1968). Fono-morfologie aromână: studiu de dialectologie structurală. București: Editura Academiei.
Caragiu Marioțeanu, Matilda (1975). Compendiu de dialectologie română (nord- și sud-dunăreană). București: Editura Științifică și Enciclopedică.
Saramandu, Nicolae (1984). Aromâna. In Rusu (ed.), Tratat de dialectologie românească. Craiova: Scrisul Românesc.
Gołąb, Zbigniew (1984). The Arumanian Dialect of Kruševo in SR Macedonia, SFR Yugoslavia. Skopje: Macedonian Academy of Sciences and Arts.
Maiden, Martin (2016). Romanian, Istro-Romanian, Megleno-Romanian, and Aromanian. In Ledgeway and Maiden (eds.), The Oxford Guide to the Romance Languages. Oxford University Press.
contrasts: seven vowels with two central ones /ɨ/ and /ə/; several varieties have only one central vowel, and the orthography writes both with ã
dental fricatives /θ ð/ and velar /ɣ/, mostly in words of Greek and Albanian origin (thimelj, dhascal)
affricates /ts dz/ and /tʃ dʒ/; /dz/ is kept where Romanian has /z/ (dzuã 'day', dzãc 'I say')
palatal sonorants /ɲ ʎ/ (njic 'small', ljepuri 'hare') and palatal stops /c ɟ/ (written ch, gh before e, i), many of them from old labials before i (ghini 'well', cheptu 'chest')
plain versus palatalised final consonant in plurals and verb forms, through final non-syllabic i
the diphthongs /e̯a/ and /o̯a/, alternating with /e/ and /o/
allophony: word-final unstressed u after a single consonant is a very short, often voiceless vowel or mere lip rounding [ᵘ] (lup [lupᵘ], om); after a consonant cluster it is a full vowel (albu, aspargu, lucru)
word-final unstressed i after a consonant is non-syllabic [ʲ], as in Romanian (lupi [lupʲ], armãnj [arˈmɨɲ])
unstressed /e/ and /o/ are raised to [i] and [u] in most varieties, and the spelling shows it (frati, casili, against Romanian frate, casele)
/x ɣ/ are palatal [ç ʝ] before front vowels (written h, y before e, i)
/r/ is an alveolar trill or tap; /l/ is clear
stops are unaspirated; /t d/ are dental
phonotactics: words that would end in a consonant usually take the short final u, so true final consonants are rarer than in Romanian
initial clusters with s plus stop plus liquid occur (strãmbu)
a prothetic a- before initial r and some other consonants is frequent (arãu 'river', aroshu 'red', armãn)

stress.rule: Stress cannot be predicted from the shape of the word; it falls on one of the last three syllables of the stem, and endings such as the definite article do not attract it (fráti, frátili).
stress.cues: duration and intensity, with pitch; vowel quality plays a part because unstressed mid vowels are raised

rhythm.vowel_reduction: moderate: unstressed e, o are raised to [i u] and final i, u are reduced to non-syllabic or whispered vowels
rhythm.notes: No rhythm measurements for Aromanian are known to us; the class is assumed from Romanian.

intonation.declarative: fall to low on the last stressed syllable (assumed from Romanian; no dedicated description found)
intonation.yes_no_question: rise after a low stressed syllable of the questioned word, with a final fall when unstressed syllables follow, as in Romanian and the neighbouring Balkan languages (assumed)
intonation.wh_question: high on the question word, then a fall (assumed)
intonation.continuation: rise at the end of non-final phrases (assumed)
intonation.accent_shape: rise through the stressed syllable before the nucleus (assumed)
intonation.notes: Aromanian intonation has not been described in the sources used here. All entries are assumptions from Romanian and should be read as low confidence.

phonation: final short u and i are often whispered (voiceless)

problems: final short u and i are full vowels (lupu [lˈupu], lupi [lˈupi]); the non-syllabic or whispered final vowels of the language are missing, unlike in the Romanian voice

stress follows a fixed rule (penultimate when the word ends in a vowel, otherwise final), so forms with endings are wrong (casili [kasˈili], fratili [fratˈili], lupilj [lupˈiʎ], oaminj [o̯amˈiɲ] for stress on the first syllable)
the letter o is always given primary stress, a heuristic that relies on the raising of unstressed o to u; it fails in newer loanwords that keep an unstressed o
ci, gi before a vowel keep a glide: ficior [fitʃjˈor], gioc [dʒjˈok], gione [dʒjˈone], where i only marks the affricate
the IPA labels of the palatal stops contain a stress mark in place of a palatal symbol (ghini prints as [gˈˈini], cheatrã as [kˈˈe̯atrə])
ã is always [ə] and â always [ɨ], as the spelling allows no better; varieties that distinguish the two central vowels cannot be served from this orthography
no tune set is selected, so the generic default tunes are used
good: the consonants that set Aromanian apart from Romanian are present: [θ ð ɣ], [ɲ ʎ], [dz], palatal stops for ch, gh
the diphthongs [e̯a] and [o̯a] are single phonemes
initial [je] in the pronouns el, ea, eu is given in the word list, and function words are marked unstressed

notes: The voice is marked as testing. The rule file is small (138 lines) and was written in 2025 by one contributor. The orthography does not mark stress, so stress needs a word list.
